doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24

title: Funeral marches and jazzing on the way back
summary: Edna and Mr. Senegal describe dead marches on the way to the grave and lively music, "glad you're dead you rascal," after burial.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Out in the country they did that too? Yeah. Like happy music?
Glad you did your rascal you. Oh, they used to do that better.
The old folks used to do that.
They used to play those dead marches. Yeah. After they're buried, the dead, then they'd come back happy. Come back with a high road.

Happy. That was at the Catholic Church too? Well, yes, because you see they were away from the church then. They'd buried the dead. The church had nothing to do. The priest was gone. Everybody was gone.

See, they played those funerals, you know, those hammers and wilders were going to the church. Going to the church. But they didn't go to the church. When the funeral went to the church. When the priest would arrive at the church, well then they wouldn't be playing anymore.

And after the funeral was over, coming back going to the graveyard, they'd play another dead march while going to the graveyard. And after they buried the dead, then they jazzed. Then they played the sand coming back.
Glad you're dead you're rascal. All kinds of things.
